passage_answers.location: sec:SIMULATING-PLACE-GENERATE, field formula and symbol paragraph
passage_answers.answer: The field h is the Gaussian input; q is dimensionless, C(0) input variance, and positive excess times gain is firing rate. This is STAR Eqs. 2–4 in translated guide notation. Threshold and local correlation scale control spatial geometry; gain controls rate units. The required Gaussian-field meanings are taught in the linked earlier place chapter.

The archive actually draws independent normal values, applies scipy.ndimage.gaussian_filter, divides each map by its own RMS, subtracts theta and clips below zero. This traces required inputs, transformations and output fields without claiming a recurrent-network implementation. The following paragraph correctly qualifies finite sampling and normalization.

Methods S2 derives a possible random-presynaptic-input origin; archived generators do not instantiate those neurons or weights. The claim that map agreement alone does not uniquely establish wiring is warranted by what was measured. No stronger causal conclusion is implied.

200 m bats use mean size/gap, 6 m bats mean size/occupied fraction, 2D mean area/count, 3D mean volume/occupied fraction. These match STAR p. e2. The wording is a summary and does not claim the same pair for every 1D dataset. Earlier place tests explain silent-cell selection and the other datasets.

passage_answers.location: sec:SIMULATING-PLACE-FIT, fitted-statistic definition and further comparisons
passage_answers.answer: The definition correctly identifies a summary used to choose parameters. Distinguishing recovery of that summary from additional distribution/shape tests is valid; the statement retains separate gain fitting, so it does not imply all further tests are parameter-free.

The article compares available-data simulated-density likelihoods/AIC/BIC with a fitted lognormal and does not report a held-out forecast. High-threshold analytical laws have a narrower regime than finite-threshold numerical comparisons. Both claims are supported; the text does not say simulations prove the limit theorem.

STAR p. e2 explicitly specifies 10^4 random-field simulations matching experimental cell count for model histogram spread. The text limits the meaning of that spread correctly and does not invent unreported full sample counts.

A small positive bridge can connect components; rectification can break a bridge; smoothing can remove peaks/fill holes. These are possible effects, correctly phrased as can rather than universal outcomes.

Consecutive bins times spatial resolution produce 1D lengths; voxel count times voxel volume produces physical 3D volume. Archived 3D methods sometimes return volume fractions, but the prose describes the physical measurement and does not falsely identify that return value. Component labeling, large-field exclusions, peak detection, finite differences, and Gudhi Betti sums agree with STAR e2–e3.

passage_answers.location: sec:SIMULATING-PLACE-MEASURE, 10 cm bins and figure summary

passage_answers.location: fold Width and edge conventions, covariance conversion
passage_answers.answer: Let C(x)=K exp[-x^2/(4b^2)]. Then C''(0)=-K/(2b^2), so -C(0)/C''(0)=2b^2 and ell=sqrt(2)b for b>0. This verifies the displayed relationship and units. The ideal continuous assumption and finite sampling/filter truncation limits are retained. This is a guide calculation from the archived smoothing operation, not a new biological fit.
